neighbours.label: a subject or copula about to receive a physical-state predicate (is plugged in, are heated, teeth extracted, screen cracked)
fire: After the fall I noticed that the phone screen was cracked across the top.
Check that the bolts on the wheel are tight before you drive off.
Two of my molars were pulled by the dentist yesterday afternoon.
Make sure the hose is firmly attached to the tap before turning it on.
Once the wires are disconnected, lift the old switch out of the box.
The hinge on the cupboard door is loose and it rattles all the time.
Wait until the glue is completely dry before you sand the joint.
The rear tyre was flat when we came back to the car park.
quiet: After the meeting I noticed that the schedule was changed for next week.
Check that the invitations are sent before you leave for the weekend.
Two of my friends were invited by the director yesterday afternoon.
Make sure the report is finished before the manager arrives.
Once the votes are counted, the chair will announce the result.
The plan for the cupboard project is vague and it worries me.
Wait until the decision is final before you tell the others.
The mood was cheerful when we came back to the office.

notes: Card: broad-ish (0.67% over 0.1 max); top examples 'wisdom teeth [extracted]', 'peripheral components [unhooked]', 'power cord is [plugged]', 'once they are [heated]'. The + pole's output suppresses loose, cracked, broken, torn, so the - pole leans toward those. Near misses use the same verbs with abstract predicates.
